builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Why Kubernetes Cannot Contain a Full Lazy-Pulling Cache: Two Impossibility Results and a Bounded, Honest Design for Model Serving
summary: The method replaces the unbounded, unaccounted node-level cache created by lazy container-image pulling (stargz-snapshotter, SOCI, Nydus) with a cache that enforces a hard byte budget keyed to filesystem truth and pass-through semantics in which a failed cache write never becomes a failed read. It costs approximately 18.5% additional completion time, requires deploying a modified snapshotter component inside the serving nodes, and adds lossy, non-blocking accounting machinery to maintain. It can fail if the workload does not actually use lazy pulling, if the lossy accounting's dropped updates misalign with real pressure in untested conditions, or if the upstream proposal is not merged and the team must maintain a fork.
rationale: The reliability gain is large and demonstrated, but it is only relevant if the reader's serving stack uses lazy image pulling on Kubernetes, so adoption must be validated against their actual deployment shape and the maintenance burden of a non-upstream component.
technique: Bounded lazy-pull cache with filesystem-truth accounting

claims.statement: The method replaces the unbounded, unaccounted node-level cache created by lazy container-image pulling (stargz-snapshotter, SOCI, Nydus) with a cache that enforces a hard byte budget keyed to filesystem truth and pass-through semantics in which a failed cache write never becomes a failed read. It costs approximately 18.5% additional completion time, requires deploying a modified snapshotter component inside the serving nodes, and adds lossy, non-blocking accounting machinery to maintain. It can fail if the workload does not actually use lazy pulling, if the lossy accounting's dropped updates misalign with real pressure in untested conditions, or if the upstream proposal is not merged and the team must maintain a fork.

Upstream stargz-snapshotter fails 273 of 280 model files at 90% cache pre-fill, while the proposed system reads all 150.3 GB with zero errors at +18.5% completion cost, holding a hard byte budget under live reads, co-tenancy, and a three-node fleet.
